name: SocialComponentClientFacet_ReceiveAvailableTitles
summary: The social facet's title list. 494-byte body: the shared two-u64 head, then TWO prefix-counted vectors of u32 BE - 109 ids and then 10 ids. The ten are a strict subset of the hundred-and-nine, which is a measured relation and not a guess; the ids themselves are per-account data, not constants of the binary (none of them occurs anywhere in .rdata in either byte order). 16 + 1 + 109*4 + 1 + 10*4 = 494 exactly, so the layout accounts for the whole body.
purpose: Tell the client which titles it can choose from and which subset of them it currently holds. What the two vectors MEAN is inferred from the message name plus the subset relation; the client struct's own member names live in runtime-built descriptors and were not read, so the fields are carried positionally.

created_when: the client's social component asks for its titles, or the server changes them
lifecycle.if_absent: the client shows no titles. The social UI has its own request paths (RequestAvailableTitles, RequestNewTitles, RequestSetTitle are named in the client's Social bus strings) but no capture shows which of them this message answers

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the wide prefix varint b3 40, i.e. type index 4147 = 0x1033. fields[] below use BODY offsets, so the first body byte is at 0x00 and the 498-byte record starts 4 bytes earlier.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured ce 81 13 6a 2b 7a d3 3e = 0xce81136a2b7ad33e. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id, the social client facet. One of the nine per-component ids the 2026-11-09 corpus scan enumerated; it appears on this wire and on no other.
fields.provenance: corpus-wide scan of 36 R records across 10 wire types, one local id per component; the head's first u64 is named in msg.time-sync-to-client.json from FUN_1416c1c40

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a. Second u64 of the shared head: the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id written big-endian.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json; re-measured here

fields.name: title_ids
fields.note: The first vector: one prefix-varint count (measured 0x6d = 109), then 109 u32 BE. All 109 are distinct. The vector reader FUN_14293d640 is generic and visible: it writes a prefix-varint count, then loops the elements through FUN_140876e70, which is the same u32 BE primitive the atlas pinned for the Territory batch - so the codec is confirmed by a second route, not inferred from the sample. The ids do not occur anywhere in .rdata in either byte order, so they are per-account data rather than binary constants. Named positionally: the card does not claim these are the titles the account can choose, only that they are this message's first id vector.
fields.provenance: capture: 0x62_T0x1033_R.bin body[0x10..0x1c4]; decompile: reader FUN_143eb0950 -> FUN_14293d640 -> FUN_140876e70

fields.name: title_selection_ids
fields.note: The second vector: one prefix-varint count (measured 0x0a = 10), then 10 u32 BE. The measured relation to title_ids is what earns this field's shape: the ten values are a STRICT SUBSET of the hundred-and-nine - all ten are found in the first vector, written in a different order (their indices there are 3, 0, 4, 1, 2, 18, 83, 92, 63, 104). A subset written out of order is a selection, not a parallel list. That is why the field is named for a selection rather than for a second independent set. What the selection MEANS - held now, unlocked, displayed - is not measured and is not claimed.
fields.provenance: capture: same body[0x1c5..0x1f2]; the subset relation measured by decoding both vectors and testing set membership and element-by-element index lookup
